cues.en: I developed a storyline for Shadow Man. He comes back at predetermined moments through the game. There's one point where he steals a potion. Just as you're about to reach it, Shadow Man comes running in, drinks it, and runs off.
cues.zh: 我为《影子人》构思了一个故事情节。他在游戏里的预设时间点会再次出现。有一个情节是他偷了一瓶药水。就在你快要拿到时，影子人跑进来喝掉了药水，然后跑开了。

cues.en: There's another moment where you're about to get through a gate. Shadow Man walks up, steps on the pressure plate, and closes the gate. At that point, you fall back down for your levels, and you're gonna have to work your way back up.
cues.zh: 还有一个情节是你正要穿过一道大门。影子人走过来，踩在压力板上，把门给关上了。那时候，你会掉回之前的关卡，不得不重新爬回来。

cues.en: These encounters were scripted to make you hate Shadow Man and see him as your enemy. So that by the time you face him with crossed swords at the end of the game, you really wanna get this guy because he set you back so many times. It's a way to build an emotional relationship between the player and an opponent through the actual gameplay rather than just telling it in a cinematic.
cues.zh: 这些遭遇战是通过脚本设计的，目的是让你讨厌影子人，把他当成敌人。这样等到游戏最后你和他兵戎相见时，你是真的想干掉这家伙，因为他之前给你添了那么多麻烦。这是一种通过实际玩法，而不是仅仅靠过场动画来建立玩家与对手之间情感联系的方式。

cues.en: Hi. I'm Jordan Mechner, creator of Prince of Persia. This is how I animated myself into a corner and had to fight my way out.
cues.zh: 大家好。我是 Jordan Mechner，《波斯王子》的创作者。这就是我是如何作茧自缚，又如何挣扎着脱困的。

cues.en: So was a kid in New York in the mid seventies. I was into comics.
cues.zh: 七十年代中期，我是纽约的一个小孩。我迷恋漫画。

cues.en: I loved movies. I grew up on Mad Magazine.
cues.zh: 我热爱电影。我是看着《疯狂》杂志长大的。

cues.en: And if computers hadn't come along when they did, you know, I might have ended up doing comics, animation.
cues.zh: 如果电脑没有在那个时候出现，你知道的，我最后可能去搞漫画或动画了。

cues.en: But when the Apple two came in 1978,
cues.zh: 但当 Apple II 在 1978 年问世时，

cues.en: I saw this as a machine that I could, first of all, use to play games at home, which was never possible before. Instead of taking rolls of 0.25 down to the local arcade, I could stay at home and play Space Invaders on the Apple two as much as I wanted. The computer was also a way that I could make my own games, and I became fascinated with that.
cues.zh: 我发现这台机器首先能让我在家里玩游戏，这以前是绝对不可能的。我不用再拿着大把的 25 美分硬币去当地的游戏机厅，而是可以待在家里，在 Apple II 上尽情地玩《太空侵略者》。电脑也是一种让我能自己制作游戏的途径，我对此着迷不已。

cues.en: This is before the Internet, so pretty much everybody was self taught. I subscribed to Creative Computing Magazine, and then a little later, Soft Talk magazine,
cues.zh: 那是互联网出现之前，所以几乎所有人都是自学成才的。我订阅了《Creative Computing》杂志，后来又订阅了《Soft Talk》杂志，

cues.en: which had articles about how to program. And then I would trade tips with my friends who are also into computers.
cues.zh: 上面有关于如何编程的文章。然后我会在喜欢电脑的朋友之间交流各种小技巧。

cues.en: So my first games were copies of existing arcade games, and you always had three lives, and the goal was to get a high score. By now, I was a freshman in college, and I wanted to do a game that would tell a story. So that's when I started programming the game that would become Carateka.
cues.zh: 所以我的第一款游戏都是对现有街机游戏的模仿，你总是有三条命，目标是获得高分。到那时，我已经是一名大学新生了，我想做一个能讲故事的游戏。也就是从那时起，我开始编写后来成为《Karateka》的游戏。

cues.en: It was a very simple story. The princess has been kidnapped by the evil warlord who's taken her to his castle. And so as the hero, you have to fight a series of karate battles with the warriors who are guarding the fortress.
cues.zh: 这是一个非常简单的故事。公主被邪恶的军阀绑架到了他的城堡。作为英雄，你需要与守护堡垒的武士们进行一系列的空手道对决。

cues.en: So you're basically running from left to right. You fight one warrior after another until you reach the end, and then you fight the the big bad guy and rescue the princess.
cues.zh: 所以你基本上就是在从左往右跑。一个接一个地击败武士，直到到达终点，然后打败终极大反派并救出公主。

cues.en: So the computer that I was working on was the Apple two. And at that time, the Apple was actually the number one game platform,
cues.zh: 我当时在上面工作的电脑是 Apple II。在那个时代，Apple 实际上是头号游戏平台，

cues.en: but it had limitations. The Apple two's music capabilities weren't that great. It only had four colors. The screen was 280 by one ninety two pixels, And everything had to fit into 48 k of memory. That was pretty much a hard limit. In those days, this was before Photoshop. This was before we had the graphics and animation tools. If you wanted to put a character up on the screen, you pretty much had to do it pixel by pixel. So when I tried to do the animation for the character, I found out pretty quickly that it just looked stiff and it didn't have the lifelike quality
cues.zh: 但它也有局限性。Apple II 的音乐功能没那么强。它只有四种颜色。屏幕分辨率是 280 乘 192 像素，而且所有东西都必须塞进 48KB 的内存里。这基本上是个死限制。在当年，Photoshop 还没诞生。在我们拥有图形和动画工具之前。如果你想在屏幕上显示一个角色，基本上得一个像素一个像素地画。所以当我尝试为角色做动画时，我很快发现它看起来很僵硬，完全没有那种

cues.en: that I was imagining in my head.
cues.zh: 我在脑海中想象的生动感。

cues.en: So I used a technique called rotoscoping,
cues.zh: 所以我用了一种叫做转描的技术，

cues.en: which actually has a long history. It goes back to the early days of film animation.
cues.zh: 这其实有着悠久的历史，可以追溯到早期电影动画时代。

cues.en: Early Disney animators used film footage as reference for the animation in in the early films. If you look at Snow White, the human characters like Snow White and the prince were actually animated using rotoscoping,
cues.zh: 早期的迪士尼动画师在早期电影中会用实拍胶片作为动画参考。如果你看过《白雪公主》，里面像白雪公主和王子这样的人类角色，其实就是用转描技术制作出来的，

cues.en: means that, the Disney animators filmed live actors doing the moves that they needed to animate on screen. And then, they would actually project these frames and copy or trace them frame by frame to create the animation that we've seen. So I did that for Carateka. I used Super eight film to film my karate teacher doing the kicks and punches and the movements that I needed the character to do on screen.
cues.zh: 这意味着，迪士尼动画师会拍摄真人演员做出银幕上所需动作的画面。然后，他们会把这些画面投射出来，逐帧进行临摹或描摹，从而创作出我们看到的动画。所以我对《空手道》也用了这招。我用超八毫米胶片拍下我的空手道老师展示踢腿、出拳以及角色在银幕上需要的各种动作。

cues.en: And then I traced each Super eight film frame with tracing paper and pencil and then translated those into pixels to get it up on the screen. That was kind of the rotoscope one point o.
cues.zh: 然后我用描图纸和铅笔描下每一格超八毫米胶片画面，再把它们转化为像素放到屏幕上。这就是某种意义上的 1.0 版转描技术。

cues.en: Karateka came out in 1984,
cues.zh: 《空手道》于 1984 年问世，

cues.en: and it became a number one bestseller.
cues.zh: 并且成了畅销榜第一名。

cues.en: So this was really lucky for me that it happened when it did because as I graduated from college, instead of going out and getting a job, I actually had the luxury of thinking, what do I wanna do next? And I had an idea to do another game. One of the inspirations was the first ten minutes of the movie Raiders of the Lost Ark.
cues.zh: 这对我来说真是太幸运了，因为它的推出时机恰到好处，当我大学毕业时，我没有去找工作，而是有余裕去思考：接下来我想做什么？我萌生了做另一款游戏的想法。其中一个灵感来源就是电影《夺宝奇兵》的前十分钟。

cues.en: If you remember, you know, Indiana Jones in the opening sequence runs, jumps over a pit, almost misses,
cues.zh: 如果你还记得，你知道的，在《夺宝奇兵》的开场片段里，印第安纳·琼斯奔跑、跳过一个深坑，差一点没过去，

cues.en: spikes spring out of the wall, you know, there's a gate that's closing.
cues.zh: 墙上弹出了尖刺，你知道的，还有一扇正在关上的门。

cues.en: And to me, like, those actions kind of matched what I was seeing in platform games like Lode Runner and the castles of Doctor. Creep, where you'd step on a pressure plate, it would open a gate. I thought, what if we combine that gameplay with a character who's so human feeling
cues.zh: 对我而言，这些动作有点符合我在平台游戏里看到的场景，比如《淘金者》和《恐怖博士的城堡》，在里头你踩上一个压力板，就会打开一扇门。我想，如果我们把这种玩法结合起来，打造一个感觉如此有人情味的角色，

cues.en: that you feel like if you miss the jump and you fall, it's really gonna hurt. Because in the early platform games, characters were kind of weightless. You know, you would jump and you you would make it or not, but you would float down to the bottom. It didn't feel like you could really get hurt. So my idea was to kind of combine
cues.zh: 让你觉得如果你没跳过去摔了，那可真会受伤。因为早期的平台游戏里，角色基本上是没有重量的。你知道的，你跳了，要么跳过去要么没过去，但你会飘落到底部。感觉不到你真的会受伤。所以我的想法是将

cues.en: the basic platform puzzle type gameplay in a sort of a modular environment with very smooth, visceral running and jumping animation that would capture the excitement of the opening minutes of Raiders of the Lost Ark.
cues.zh: 基础的平台解谜类玩法和模块化环境结合起来，配上非常流畅、有血有肉的跑跳动画，以此捕捉到《夺宝奇兵》开场几分钟那种惊险刺激的感觉。

cues.en: The
cues.zh: 《波斯王子》的

cues.en: story of Prince of Persia was also simple.
cues.zh: 故事也很简单。

cues.en: Like caretaker, it involved rescuing a princess.
cues.zh: 就像《看护人》一样，它涉及拯救一位公主。

cues.en: And it was really inspired by the thousand and one knights and by movies like the nineteen forty Thief of Baghdad in which an evil grand vizier has seized power and imprisoned the princess.
cues.zh: 它的灵感确实来自于《一千零一夜》以及像1940年版《巴格达大盗》这样的电影，片中一个邪恶的大维齐尔夺取了权力并囚禁了公主。

cues.en: For Prince of Persia, I knew I was gonna need so much more animation.
cues.zh: 对于《波斯王子》，我知道我需要多得多的动画。

cues.en: Running, jumping, climbing, falling, all the movements that the little character would have to do on screen. And by the time I did the animation for Prince of Persia in '85, a new technology had come along, VHS. So using, one of the early VHS cameras, I videotaped my brother running and jumping and doing all those things in the parking lot across the street from our high school. Go.
cues.zh: 奔跑、跳跃、攀爬、跌落，所有这些小角色在屏幕上必须完成的动作。等到我在 85 年制作《波斯王子》的动画时，一项新技术出现了，那就是 VHS 录像带。于是我利用早期的 VHS 摄像机之一，把我的兄弟在街对面我们高中停车场里跑步、跳跃以及做所有这些动作的过程录了下来。走。

cues.en: Jump.
cues.zh: 跳。

cues.en: Action.
cues.zh: 动作。

cues.en: Stop.
cues.zh: 停。

cues.en: Get up. Get up. Get up. And then the problem was how to get these videotaped frames into the computer. After a bit of trial and error, the technique that I finally settled on for Prince of Persia was a kind of a analog to digital to analog to digital. It involved several steps. I took the videotape of my brother and put that on a TV screen in a darkened room, put a 35 millimeter film camera on a tripod, aimed it at the TV screen, and then took a picture. Did a frame advance on the VCR, took another picture. Frame advance,
cues.zh: 起来。起来。起来。然后问题变成了如何把这些录像帧放进电脑里。经过一番摸索后，我最终为《波斯王子》确定的技术是一种类似于“模拟转数字、再转模拟、再转数字”的过程。这包含了几个步骤。我把记录了我兄弟的录像带放进暗室里的电视机，把一台 35 毫米胶片相机架在三脚架上，对准电视机，然后拍下一张照片。在 VCR 上前进一帧，再拍一张照片。前进一帧，

cues.en: frame advance, frame advance. Then I took that roll of film containing about 35 frames down to the local photo mat, the one hour photo, had the film developed, and then got back a sheaf of snapshots,
cues.zh: 前进一帧，前进一帧。然后我把那卷包含大约 35 帧画面的胶卷带到当地的照相馆，也就是那个一小时冲印店，把胶卷冲洗出来，拿到了一叠快照，

cues.en: which I then scotch taped together and using a a Sharpie
cues.zh: 接着我用透明胶带把它们粘在一起，并用一支签字笔

cues.en: and white out, highlighted the outlines of each character, then put that on a Xerox machine and came out with one clean sheet of paper with a series of frames of a clean white character against a black background.
cues.zh: 和修正液勾勒出每个角色的轮廓，再把它放到复印件上，最后得到了一张干净的纸，上面印着一系列黑底白字的清晰角色帧。

cues.en: So that contrast was sharp enough that I could then put that piece of paper on an animation stand, pointed a video camera at it, and ran that into the Apple two, which had no video in. This was a special digitizer card that could get one clean still image. It couldn't capture motion. But once I had that sheet of nine or 12 individual frames of the character, I could then go in pixel by pixel and cut them out on screen using my animation tool and then run those frames in sequence. And so all of this took weeks of work to get from that videotape run or jump to the point where the game was actually playing back those frames in sequence on screen.
cues.zh: 所以这种对比足够鲜明，我才能把那张纸放到动画台上，用摄像机对准它，再把信号输入Apple II，而它本身没有视频输入。这是一块特殊的数字化卡，能获取一张干净静止图像，但无法捕捉运动。不过一旦我有那张包含角色9到12个独立帧的纸，我就可以用动画工具在屏幕上逐像素抠出来，然后按顺序播放这些帧。所以所有这些花了数周时间，从录像带上的跑或跳，到游戏实际在屏幕上按顺序回放这些帧。

cues.en: When I first saw that character running and jumping on the screen, it had that rough illusion of life and of weight. But these were the days of eight bit graphics. Each frame of animation in Prince of Persia was a series of bytes that represented a fixed image on the screen. And then the next frame of animation was another set of bytes. So to do something like jump in place took 12 frames. To do a running jump might take 15 frames. And the number of frames made the animation smoother.
cues.zh: 当我第一次看到那个角色在屏幕上跑和跳时，它有一种粗糙的生动感和重量感。但那是八位图形时代。《波斯王子》中每帧动画都是一系列字节，代表屏幕上固定图像，然后下一帧动画是另一组字节。所以像原地跳跃要12帧，跑跳可能要15帧。帧数让动画更平滑。

cues.en: So once you add the jumping, the running, the turning, the hanging, the swinging, all of these things, each individual movement took memory. This is where one difference between computers then and now became very important because the Apple II's memory was
cues.zh: 所以一旦加上跳跃、奔跑、转身、悬挂、摆动，所有这些，每个单独动作都耗内存。这就是当时和现在计算机的一个区别变得非常重要，因为Apple II的内存是

cues.en: 48 k. That's less than a normal text email. So that had to contain everything.
cues.zh: 48k。比一封普通文本邮件还少。所以它必须容纳一切。

cues.en: All of the images, all of the backgrounds, all of the frames of animation, all of the logic to make it work, all of the sound effects, all of the music,
cues.zh: 所有图像、所有背景、所有动画帧、让它运转的所有逻辑、所有音效、所有音乐，

cues.en: everything. So with all the basic animations that the character needed to navigate through the dungeon, that had filled up all of the computer's available memory.
cues.zh: 一切。角色在地牢中穿行所需的所有基础动画，已经填满了电脑的全部可用内存。

cues.en: So it was June 1988, and I was two years into making Prince of Persia. And at this point, I'd done most of the heavy lifting to get the game working. I had a smoothly animated character that was running through these dungeons,
cues.zh: 那是1988年6月，我制作《波斯王子》已经两年了。到这时，我已经完成了让游戏运转的大部分繁重工作。我有一个流畅动画的角色，在地牢中奔跑，

cues.en: climbing and falling and stepping on pressure plates to open gates and jumping over pits, almost falling on spikes. Everybody who saw the game, ooed and odd, it was like a great proof of concept. But it wasn't that much fun to play. And I kind of had the sinking feeling as I realized, like, I've done almost everything I meant to do, but it it just doesn't have that excitement that I was hoping for.
cues.zh: 攀爬、坠落、踩压力板开门、跳过深坑，差点掉在尖刺上。每个看到游戏的人都惊叹不已，这就像是一个极佳的概念验证。但玩起来并没有那么有趣。我隐隐有一种不安的感觉，因为我意识到，我几乎做完了所有想做的事，但它就是没有我期望的那种兴奋感。

cues.en: Also, there was a ticking clock, which is that the Apple two platform was dying. When I started to make Prince of Persia, the Apple two was still the number one games platform. By 1988, there were new machines that were coming out that had more colors,
cues.zh: 而且，还有一个紧迫的时间问题，那就是Apple II平台正在消亡。当我开始制作《波斯王子》时，Apple II还是第一大游戏平台。到了1988年，新机器纷纷问世，它们有更多颜色、

cues.en: higher resolution,
cues.zh: 更高分辨率、

cues.en: better sound capability, and I was really at the tail end of the Apple II's life cycle, but I felt that switching to a different platform would have been like starting over. So the worry was that I could come out with a game that was great, that was fun, but nobody would ever play it.
cues.zh: 更好的声音能力，而我真的处在Apple II生命周期的尾声，但我觉得换到另一个平台就像从头开始。所以担忧的是，我可能做出一款很棒、很好玩的游戏，却没人会去玩它。

cues.en: You know, it's always a problem when you reach a point in development that makes you question your initial vision. Sometimes the answer is to say,
cues.zh: 你知道，在开发过程中总会遇到让你质疑最初构想的时刻。有时答案是，

cues.en: you know, just believe in the initial vision, execute it, it's gonna be fine. But sometimes you discover things along the way that make you realize that the initial vision is just a first draft.
cues.zh: 就是相信最初的构想，去执行它，会没事的。但有时你会在过程中发现一些事情，让你意识到最初的构想只是个初稿。

cues.en: From the beginning, I had the idea that the main character would not fight, that this was a nonviolent character just trying to survive in a dungeon, in a violent world. That is, there are spikes that spring out of the floor. There's, you know, gates and falling blocks that can crush you.
cues.zh: 从一开始，我就设想主角不会战斗，这是一个非暴力的角色，只是试图在地牢中、在一个暴力的世界里生存。也就是说，有从地板弹出的尖刺。还有门和掉落的方块能把你压碎。

cues.en: But this is not a violent character. The point is just to get through these traps and get to the end and rescue the princess. And I had used all of the resources that the Apple two offered to try to create this. I didn't have room to put in another character.
cues.zh: 但这不是个暴力角色。目标只是穿过这些陷阱到达终点，救出公主。我用尽了Apple II提供的所有资源来尝试实现这个。我没有空间再加入另一个角色了。

cues.en: So I was sharing an office with friends who were also working on their own projects. Robert Cook was working on a game that became D Generation. Tomi Pierce was creating educational software. And every time Tomi saw Prince of Persia on my screen as she walked by my desk, she would say, combat. Combat. Combat. You need combat or this game's not gonna be fun. And this frustrated me because I hadn't planned for combat. Karateka was a fighting game. The whole game was you meet a guard, you fight the guard, and then on to the next battle. And so I would explain to Tomei, I can't do that because there's not enough memory in the computer to also have a smoothly animated enemy that does everything that I would need an enemy to do. But when Tome got an idea, she wouldn't let it go. And so I would add a new feature to the game and say, okay. Now now there's torches on the wall. Now I've got jaw traps that chomp and add suspense. Isn't it better now? Tomi would look at the new feature I'd added and say, combat, combat, combat.
cues.zh: 所以我当时和也在做各自项目的朋友们共用一间办公室。Robert Cook在做一款后来成为D Generation的游戏。Tomi Pierce在做教育软件。每次Tomi路过我桌子看到屏幕上的《波斯王子》时，她都会说，战斗。战斗。战斗。你需要战斗，不然这游戏不会好玩。这让我很沮丧，因为我没规划过战斗。《空手道ka》是个格斗游戏。整个游戏就是你遇到守卫，和守卫打，然后进入下一场战斗。所以我会跟Tomi解释，我做不到，因为电脑内存不够再放一个流畅动画的敌人，来做一个敌人需要做的所有事情。但Tomi一旦有了想法，就不会放手。所以我会给游戏加个新功能然后说，好了。现在墙上有火把了。现在我有会咬合的颌夹陷阱来增加悬念。现在是不是更好了？Tomi会看着我加的新功能说，战斗，战斗，战斗。

cues.en: And with frustration, I realized that there was something to what she was saying. As much as I wished that it was almost done, it just wasn't that much fun. So this was the problem. Two years into development, I had used up all the memory to get as far as I'd gotten, but the game was missing that suspense and excitement and sense of conflict that had made Karateka so simple and so much fun. What was I gonna do?
cues.zh: 我沮丧地意识到，她说的话有几分道理。尽管我希望能快完成了，但游戏确实没那么好玩。问题就在这儿。开发两年了，我把所有内存都用在了已实现的部分上，但游戏缺少那种悬念、刺激和冲突感——正是这些让《空手道》变得简单又好玩。我该怎么办？

cues.en: So I can tell you exactly what happened on that day in June 1988 because I wrote about it in my journal. It was another day in which,
cues.zh: 所以我能确切告诉你1988年6月那天发生了什么，因为我写在了日记里。那是又一天，

cues.en: Tommy had come and looked at my screen and said, combat.
cues.zh: 汤米过来看了看我的屏幕，说，战斗。

cues.en: You need combat. And again, I'd rolled out my usual argument about how, first of all, that's not the concept of the game. Second of all, there's no memory.
cues.zh: 你需要战斗。我又搬出老一套的论据：首先，这不符合游戏的概念。其次，没有内存了。

cues.en: And she said, well, in Karateka, you used the same shapes for the hero and the enemy. Couldn't you do that? I said, no. Because the hero looks like a likable,
cues.zh: 她说，在《空手道》里，主角和敌人用的是一样的形状。你不能那样做吗？我说，不行。因为主角看起来是个讨喜的、

cues.en: endearing kind of, character. The enemy shouldn't look like that. And she said, well, what if you made enemies a different color? And then the idea came to me. What if I exclusive or ed each bite with itself shifted one bit over?
cues.zh: 可爱的角色。敌人不该长那样。她说，那如果让敌人换个颜色呢？然后我有了个主意。如果我把每个字节与自身右移一位做异或运算呢？

cues.en: So the Apple two didn't have image processing in any kind of sense that we understand it now because the graphics were all bit mapped. But one of the assembly language instructions was called exclusive or, which basically means if the two bits are the same, you get a zero. If the two bits are different, you get a one. So as I was telling Tomi for the tenth time why I couldn't, draw a character in a different color than the one I'd originally created, I realized that if I used the exclusive or instruction shifted one bit over, this would create a kind of a shimmery ghostly outline of the main character. And as soon as I said those words, the character's name popped into being, Shadow Man. So with Tomi and Robert looking over my shoulder, it actually took me all of five minutes to write the code that would turn the main character into a shimmery,
cues.zh: Apple II 并没有我们现在理解的任何意义上的图像处理，因为图形全是位图。但有一条汇编指令叫异或，意思是如果两位相同就得零，两位不同就得一。所以当我第十次跟汤米解释为什么我不能把角色画成和最初创建时不同的颜色时，我意识到，如果我用异或指令移一位，就能给主角创造出一种闪烁的幽灵般轮廓。我一说出这些话，角色的名字就蹦了出来：暗影人。于是汤米和罗伯特在我身后看着，我实际上只花了五分钟就写出了把主角变成闪烁的、

cues.en: ghostly version of itself. And as soon as we saw Shadow Man running, jumping, and climbing through the dungeon,
cues.zh: 幽灵般版本的代码。我们一看到暗影人在地牢里奔跑、跳跃、攀爬，

cues.en: it became obvious that this was this was the opponent that the game needed.
cues.zh: 就明显感觉到，这正是游戏需要的对手。

cues.en: It was Robert who suggested that Shadow Man could come into being when you jump through a mirror. Your ghostly self jumps out the other direction, and then once it's loose in the dungeons, becomes your enemy, stealing potions, closing gates that you wanted open, and just kind of wreaking all kind of havoc. So out of necessity
cues.zh: 是Robert提议说，当你穿过镜子时，Shadow Man 就可以诞生。你的幽灵自我从另一边跳出来，一旦它在地下城里脱了缰，就成了你的敌人：偷你的药水，关上你想打开的门，各种搞破坏。于是出于无奈

cues.en: was born this character who ended up becoming one of the best features of the game. It's a case of where constraints
cues.zh: 这个角色就这样诞生了，最终成了游戏里最出色的设计之一。这就是一个例子，说明限制

cues.en: can sometimes push you to more creative solutions than you would have found in the beginning if they had been available.
cues.zh: 有时候反而能把你推向更有创意的解决方案，比一开始条件齐备时你能想出来的还要好。

cues.en: If memory had not been a constraint, I probably would have created all kinds of monsters and enemies in Prince of Persia to add a lot of variety. But because there was no room for any of that, I was forced to dig deeper and came up with Shadow Man, which ended up actually being kind of deeper and more satisfying.
cues.zh: 如果内存不是限制，我大概会在《波斯王子》里做出各种各样的怪物和敌人，增加很多变化。但因为根本放不下这些东西，我被迫往深处挖，才想出了 Shadow Man，结果它反而更有深度、更让人满足。

cues.en: At the end of the game, when you confront your shadow self and you fight him with swords, every time you hit Shadow Man, you lose a strength point. You realize that if you keep fighting, you're eventually gonna kill yourself. So the solution is not to win the sword fight, but to put away your sword. And when you put away the sword, Shadow Man does the same. And then facing each other, you run towards Shadow Man, he runs towards you, and the two of you merge and are reunited. And then you get back all the health points that Shadow Man had stolen from you throughout the game. And with this restored strength and wholeness, you're then able to fight the Grand Vizier and win the game. That's something that I wouldn't have come up with if I didn't have to.
cues.zh: 游戏最后，你面对自己的影子自我，和他用剑决斗。每次你击中 Shadow Man，就失去一点力量值。你会意识到，如果一直打下去，最终杀掉的是你自己。所以解法不是赢下这场剑斗，而是收起你的剑。当你收起剑，Shadow Man 也照做。然后你们面对面，你朝他跑过去，他也朝你跑过来，两人合二为一、重新合一。接着你拿回了 Shadow Man 在整个游戏里从你身上偷走的所有生命值。带着这份恢复的力量与完整，你才能去打败大维齐尔，通关游戏。这是我如果不是被逼着，根本想不出来的点子。

cues.en: Once Shadowman was in the game, it was obvious that that was the right way to go. And so I managed to squeeze out of the memory enough frames to do sword fighting so that you could fight the shadow version of yourself. And that was so compelling that I said, alright. Whatever it takes, I've got to find a way to populate this dungeon with guards. And at this late stage, I found a way to take 12 k of memory that was hiding in the auxiliary memory card of the Apple two to add a guard. But this presented a new problem.
cues.zh: Shadowman 加入游戏后，很明显这就是正确的方向。于是我从内存里挤出了足够的帧数来做剑斗，让你能和自己影子版本的对手交战。这太有吸引力了，我就说，好吧。不管付出什么代价，我都得想办法给这个地牢填满守卫。在这个后期阶段，我找到办法，利用 Apple II 辅助内存卡里藏着的 12K 内存来加一个守卫。但这也带来了新问题。

cues.en: How do we create the animation for the enemies? So the model for the animations in Prince of Persia had been my younger brother, who at this point was 3,000 miles away, and he wasn't any good at sword fighting anyway. So my first attempt was to film myself and my office mate, Robert, with a sword doing fencing.
cues.zh: 我们怎么给敌人做动画？《波斯王子》动画的模特一直是我弟弟，而他现在在 3000 英里之外，况且他本来也不擅长剑斗。所以我最初的尝试是拍下我自己和同事 Robert 拿着剑比划击剑。

cues.en: Unfortunately,
cues.zh: 不幸的是，

cues.en: that didn't work.
cues.zh: 那没成功。

cues.en: Finally, in desperation, I turned to one of my favorite films, the 1938 Robin Hood with Errol Flynn. And it just happened that in this film, in his climactic duel with Basil Rathbone, there's a sequence of about six seconds where two characters are perfectly in profile fighting each other. So with a VHS tape of the 1938 Robin Hood, I took photographs of each frame of film and extracted the moves that the characters would need to do in order to do sword fighting. And once the guards were in there, the game felt complete. Now, as you move through the dungeons, you had that feeling of challenge, of suspense, of fear that had been such an important part of what made Karateka successful.
cues.zh: 最后，走投无路之下，我想到了我最喜欢的电影之一，1938 年 Errol Flynn 主演的《罗宾汉》。恰好在这部电影里，他与 Basil Rathbone 的高潮决斗中，有大约六秒的片段，两个角色完全以侧面轮廓互相打斗。于是我拿着一盘 1938 年《罗宾汉》的 VHS 录像带，逐帧拍照，提取出角色做剑斗所需的动作。守卫一加进去，游戏就完整了。现在，当你在地牢中穿行时，会有那种挑战、悬疑、恐惧的感觉，而正是这些让《空手道》大获成功。

cues.en: The lesson, if there is one, you know, the best way that I've been able to formulate it, is that when you have these two voices, you know, two different approaches in your brain giving you two different solutions that are diametrically opposed, to really try to tune in to each voice and think, is this the voice, you know, of the big picture? Because sometimes you can have great ideas that are kind of taking you off the path of what you originally set out to do. But sometimes that voice is actually putting you back on the path. The reason that Shadow Man was the right thing to do, I think goes back to the original inspiration of Prince of Persia. It's basically the modern version of a swashbuckling movie. And in those old swashbuckling movies, whether it was Errol Flynn or Douglas Fairbanks
cues.zh: 如果说能从中吸取什么教训的话，你知道，我能总结出的最好方式就是：当你的脑海里出现这两种声音、也就是两种截然不同且针锋相对的解决方案时，一定要试着去聆听每一个声音，并思考：这会是从宏观大局出发的声音吗？因为有时你确实会有一些好点子，它们却会带你偏离最初设定的目标。但有时，那个声音其实是在把你带回正轨。我觉得，Shadow Man 是正确的决定，这可以追溯到《波斯王子》最初的灵感。它基本上就是一部斗剑冒险片的现代版。而在那些老派的斗剑冒险片里，不管是 Errol Flynn、Douglas Fairbanks

cues.en: or Indiana Jones, the hero did fight. So it's completely in line with that spirit.
cues.zh: 还是印第安纳·琼斯，英雄都是会战斗的。所以这完全符合那种精神。

cues.en: Prince of Persia released at the end of nineteen eighty nine on the Apple Apple two,
cues.zh: 《波斯王子》于 1989 年底在 Apple II 上发布，

cues.en: and as I'd feared, I had lost the race against time. By then, the Apple two was a dying platform. And for about a year, I had the agonizing experience of feeling that this game that I'd worked so hard on, which everybody who played was enjoying,
cues.zh: 正如我所担心的那样，我输给了时间。当时，Apple II 已经是一个日薄西山的平台。在大约一年的时间里，我经历了一种痛苦的折磨：我觉得这款我倾注了无数心血、而且每个玩过的人都很喜欢的游戏，

cues.en: that this game was gonna sink without a trace.
cues.zh: 可能会就这样悄无声息地沉没。

cues.en: What saved it was the ports to other platforms, to the PC, to the Mac, and also to consoles like Sega and Nintendo that came out over the next couple of years and kind of rescued this game that had been a flop and made it into a hit. And that's what actually made it really clear to me that adding Shadow Man in combat had been the right thing to do. Because on these other platforms,
cues.zh: 拯救它的是移植到其他平台——PC、Mac，以及在接下来的几年里推出的世嘉和任天堂等主机平台，它们拯救了这款曾经的失利之作，将其变成了热门爆款。也正是这一点，让我真正看清了：加入 Shadow Man 和战斗系统是完全正确的决定。因为在这些其他平台上，

cues.en: the memory issues that had been so critical on the Apple two no longer existed.
cues.zh: 在 Apple II 上曾至关重要的内存问题不复存在了。

cues.en: Those swashbuckling cinematic roots turned out to be a key part of, you know, what made Prince of Persia what it is.
cues.zh: 那些侠盗冒险电影式的根源，后来成了造就 Prince of Persia 如今样貌的关键部分。

cues.en: Prince of Persia was successful enough on PC that we did a sequel, Prince of Persia two, The Shadow and the Flame. And by the time this game came out in 1993,
cues.zh: Prince of Persia 在 PC 上足够成功，所以我们做了续作 Prince of Persia 2: The Shadow and the Flame。到 1993 年这款游戏推出时，

cues.en: we had a new generation of PCs
cues.zh: 我们已经有新一代 PC，

cues.en: that could do sound and music and color graphics way beyond what was possible
cues.zh: 能实现声音、音乐和彩色图形，远远超出

cues.en: in the late eighties. And we took advantage of this, adding more enemies, more characters,
cues.zh: 八十年代末所能做到的水平。我们利用了这一点，加入更多敌人、更多角色，

cues.en: and richer environments, sending the prince on a journey across a world that got us out of the dungeon and palace of Prince of Persia one. But the basic gameplay, the formula of traps, fight and flight, puzzle solving, and combat and exploration
cues.zh: 以及更丰富的环境，让王子踏上穿越世界的旅程，带我们走出 Prince of Persia 1 的地牢和宫殿。但基础玩法——陷阱、战斗与逃跑、解谜，以及战斗和探索的公式

cues.en: was still pretty close to what it had been in Prince of Persia one. Since the original Prince of Persia, the technology has advanced, but the basic questions of game design haven't really changed all that much. When we did the remake in 2003,
cues.zh: 仍然和 Prince of Persia 1 里非常接近。从初代 Prince of Persia 以来，技术进步了，但游戏设计的基本问题其实没怎么变。2003 年我们做重制版时，

cues.en: Prince of Persia, The Sands of Time, we were working on a much later generation of console, the PlayStation two generation. And so for the first time, we had three d graphics,
cues.zh: 也就是 Prince of Persia: The Sands of Time，我们是在晚得多的主机世代上开发，也就是 PlayStation 2 世代。于是我们第一次有了 3D 图形，

cues.en: the ability to rewind time,
cues.zh: 倒转时间的能力，

cues.en: sound music, you know, all these things that the Apple two couldn't do. But we still had constraints. The first draft of the story for The Sands of Time had been much more complicated with kind of this political intrigue and, you know, different factions within the kingdom. So for the final game, we ended up stripping
cues.zh: 声音、音乐，你知道，这些 Apple II 做不到的东西。但我们仍有约束。The Sands of Time 的故事初稿要复杂得多，有那种政治阴谋，还有王国里的不同派系。所以到最终游戏里，我们最终剥掉了

cues.en: all of that out and going with a much simpler story in which everybody in the kingdom has been transformed into sand monsters. And that one decision made it possible to design a game that was actually in sync with what you could do with a controller in your hands because everybody that you met was a sand monster. So your only options really were acrobatics,
cues.zh: 所有这些，改用一个简单得多的故事：王国里所有人都变成了沙怪。而那个决定让游戏设计能真正和手里的手柄操作同步，因为你遇到的每个人都是沙怪。所以你的选择其实只有杂技、

cues.en: combat,
cues.zh: 战斗、

cues.en: and running away. And that was a good fit with what you could do as a player. Even though we had the ability to do dialogue
cues.zh: 和逃跑。这和你作为玩家能做的事很契合。尽管我们有能力做对话

cues.en: and facial animations and so forth, having a large cast of characters would have taken the game away from its strengths.
cues.zh: 和面部动画等等，但让一大群角色登场反而会让游戏偏离它的强项。

cues.en: So in designing a game story, you really want to find choices that emphasize the strengths
cues.zh: 所以设计游戏故事时，你确实要找那些能突出优势的选择

cues.en: rather than emphasizing the weaknesses.
cues.zh: 而不是突出劣势。

cues.en: This year is the thirtieth anniversary
cues.zh: 今年是三十周年

cues.en: of the original Prince of Persia.
cues.zh: 原版《波斯王子》的。

cues.en: And a lot of what I've told you today, remember thanks to the fact that I kept the journal. So we're actually rereleasing these journals as a book for Prince of Persia's thirtieth anniversary. They're the journals that I kept at the time as I was making the game. So it's got the roller coaster of all the ups and downs of this game is gonna be great. This game is gonna be a disaster. And how do I solve this particular problem? We've also illustrated the journals with screenshots of the work in progress and sketches. So it's been a lot of fun for me on this anniversary
cues.zh: 我今天讲的很多内容，记住，都多亏我记了日志。所以借着《波斯王子》三十周年，我们其实正把这些日志作为一本书重新出版。它们是我当年制作游戏时记的日志。所以里面有过山车般的起起落落：这游戏会很棒。这游戏会是一场灾难。这个具体问题我要怎么解决？我们还用开发中的截图和草图给日志配了插图。所以在这个周年纪念，对我来说，这件事很有意思：

cues.en: to have a reason to go back and look at those old journals again, which,
cues.zh: 能有个理由回去再看那些旧日志，而这些日志，

cues.en: you know, being in the eighties are, you know, mostly on pen and paper.
cues.zh: 你知道，是八十年代的，你知道，大多都是纸笔。
